subject: Re: Kickoff: DPAM for private personalization
body:
Status. Csilla's DPALS run on the internal matrix-completion benchmark hit the March milestone late but clean — at epsilon=8 we're within 2.1% of the non-private baseline on held-out RMSE, using DP least squares for the linear encoder per Algorithm 1.

The risk I want visible: distribution skew. Our partner traffic is heavily skewed — a small set of power users contributes most observations — and the multi-task-under-skew analysis from the second paper says uniform per-user clipping over-penalizes exactly those users. My translation: if we keep naive clipping, encoder quality drops noticeably for the head of the distribution; the skew-aware budget split recovers most of it but adds a preprocessing pass Rosa hasn't scoped yet.

Recommend we accept a one-week slip on the May milestone to land skew-aware clipping properly rather than patch it after handoff.

Wei
